judgements.justification: A's only confidence-4 reviewer, x8VX, wrote the most specific review and scored 8; A's two-sentence meta-review never mentions it and follows the 6.5 mean of three thin 6s to a poster.
Both committees raised the same gaps (no baseline, qualitative results, scaling), and the rebuttal moved scores in both (7pq7 and 4Rfw in A, d46C in B).
A's lone 8 stood above three 6s but did not set A's tier, and A's other scores (6, 6, 6) do not match B's 7s; B has no outlier.
A's outlier x8VX replied after the rebuttal ('I maintain my favorable appreciation'); B has no outlier.
Neither committee had a low-scoring detractor; A's lowest scores were three 6s that the area chair followed, not set aside.
No reviewer or area chair on either side raised audience breadth or venue fit.
A's meta-review omits x8VX but misstates nothing; B's meta-review reports its reviewers' agreement and requested revisions accurately.
In A three of four reviewers replied (7pq7, 4Rfw, x8VX) and in B three of four did (QSy5, d46C, czKb); neither committee's majority left the rebuttal unanswered.
A's non-expert 7pq7 gave 6, not a clear accept; in B the checked reviews of naZJ and czKb already gave 7, and without QSy5's thin 8 B's mean is still 7.0.
Neither committee split evenly between accept and reject; all eight scores are 6 or above.
The notes show the same author arguments to both committees (no hybrid baseline exists, cost explanations); no difference in substance.
5o85's 'not new' verdict is correct per the paper (it generalizes Archambeau et al. and Opper and Sanguinetti); no novelty verdict rested on wrong prior work.
B's spotlight gives no argument beyond scores, but its unanimous 7-8 scores (mean 7.25) support that tier, so the tier is not above what the scores support.
No reviewer objected to the paper's framing from a neighbouring field's premises; objections concerned baselines, scaling and parameter bias.
A, the lower-tier committee, had the engaged champion (x8VX, 8, replied); B's higher tier came from four 7-8 scores, not from a champion that A lacked.
Neither committee rejected the paper or judged promised fixes too large; both accepted it.
Both area chairs based their recommendations on the visible reviews and scores; no off-record input is noted.
Both committees applied the same expectation of baselines and quantitative results and named its absence; they differed in how much it weighed, not in the standard.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score; A's lowest scores are 6 (marginally above) and rest on shared, central concerns such as missing baselines.
